Goal: add a new standalone tool `jsonl-lint` as an npm workspace under `packages/jsonl-lint/` and open one PR that meets every acceptance line of https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102. Right now `packages/` does not exist; the root `package.json` already has `"workspaces": ["packages/*"]`, and the root `npm test` runs `npm test --workspaces --if-present`. CI (`.github/workflows/test.yml`) runs `npm ci` and then `npm test` on Node 22.

Acceptance lines (each must hold at the PR head):
1. "packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> prints <file>:<line>: <error> for every row that is not valid JSON (1-based lines, blank lines skipped, an unterminated last line checked) and exits 1 if any, 0 if none"
2. "A missing file or no argument prints to stderr and exits 2"
3. "packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js exports lint(text) returning [{ line, error }]"
4. "The workspace has its own package.json (jsonl-lint, type module, test script node --test), no runtime dependencies, and node:test tests for a clean file, a bad middle row, a torn last row, blank lines and the exit codes"
5. "packages/jsonl-lint/README.md exists and the root README lists the tool"
6. "The change is one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body says Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102, and npm test and the test workflow are green at its head"

Steps:
1. Create `packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js`: a plain ES module with a named export `lint(text)`. Split the text on `\n` (also strip a trailing `\r` from each row so CRLF files work). Line numbers are 1-based. Skip rows that are empty or whitespace-only. Run `JSON.parse` on every other row, including a last row that has no trailing newline (a torn/unterminated last row must be reported if it is not valid JSON). A trailing newline at end of file must not produce an extra row. Return an array of `{ line, error }` objects, `line` a number and `error` the non-empty parse error message string, in line order; return `[]` for a clean text.
2. Create `packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js` with a `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang (make it executable, `chmod +x`). It takes one argument, the file path. With no argument: print a usage message to stderr and exit 2. If the file cannot be read (missing, etc.): print an error message to stderr and exit 2. Otherwise read it as UTF-8, call `lint`, print one line per error to stdout in exactly the form `<file>:<line>: <error>` where `<file>` is the argument exactly as given, and exit 1 if there was at least one error, 0 if none (print nothing to stdout for a clean file). Import `lint` from `../src/index.js`.
3. Create `packages/jsonl-lint/package.json` with `"name": "jsonl-lint"`, a version, `"private": true`, `"type": "module"`, `"bin": { "jsonl-lint": "bin/jsonl-lint.js" }`, `"engines": { "node": ">=22" }`, and `"scripts": { "test": "node --test" }`. No `dependencies` (and no devDependencies needed). Use only Node built-ins.
4. Write `node:test` tests under `packages/jsonl-lint/test/` (files named `*.test.js` so `node --test` discovers them), using `node:assert/strict`. Cover, as separately named tests: a clean file (lint returns `[]`, CLI exits 0 with no output); a bad middle row (reported with the right 1-based line); a torn last row with no trailing newline (reported); blank lines (skipped but still counted for numbering, so an error after blank lines has the right line number); and the exit codes 0, 1 and 2 (run the bin with `child_process.spawnSync(process.execPath, [binPath, ...])`, writing fixture files into a temp dir from `fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), ...))`; check exit 2 for both a missing file and no argument, and that stderr is non-empty in those cases; check the stdout format `<file>:<line>: <error>` for exit 1). Resolve the bin path from `import.meta.url` so tests work from any cwd.
5. Write `packages/jsonl-lint/README.md`: what the tool does, usage (`node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file>`), output format, exit codes (0 clean, 1 invalid rows, 2 missing file or no argument), the `lint(text)` API, and how to run tests.
6. Update the root `README.md`: under "What is here", replace the "No tools yet" bullet with a bullet listing `packages/jsonl-lint` and a one-line description.
7. From the repo root run `npm install` so `package-lock.json` gets the new workspace entry (CI uses `npm ci`, which fails if the lockfile is out of sync). Commit the updated `package-lock.json`. Do not commit `node_modules`.
8. Verify locally from the repo root: `npm ci && npm test` must exit 0 and show your jsonl-lint tests passing. Also try the CLI by hand: a file containing `{"a":1}`, an empty line, `{bad`, `[1,2]`, an empty line and an unterminated `{"x":` (no final newline) must print exactly two lines, for lines 3 and 6, and exit 1.
9. Commit, push, and open exactly one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body contains the line `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102` and briefly lists what was added. Do not open a second PR; if you need fixes, push to the same branch.
10. Wait for the `test` workflow to finish on the PR head commit and confirm it is green (e.g. `gh api repos/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/commits/<head-sha>/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[] | {name, status, conclusion}]'`). If it fails, read the log, fix, push, and wait again until it is green.
result.verifier:
Check the PR for https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102 at its head commit. Check out the PR head, then from the repository root run `npm ci` once before the checks. Run every command below from the repository root, in one bash shell so `$d` stays set. Report PASS or FAIL for each of the six checks, in order, with the output that decided it.

Setup (run first):
```
d=$(mktemp -d)
printf '{"a":1}\n\n{bad\n[1,2]\n\n{"x":' > "$d/bad.jsonl"
printf '{"a":1}\n\n[2]\n"s"\n' > "$d/clean.jsonl"
printf '{"a":1}\n{"b":2}' > "$d/clean-noeol.jsonl"
```
`bad.jsonl` has invalid rows at line 3 (`{bad`) and line 6 (unterminated `{"x":` with no final newline); lines 2 and 5 are blank; lines 1 and 4 are valid.

Check 1 — expect line: "packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> prints <file>:<line>: <error> for every row that is not valid JSON (1-based lines, blank lines skipped, an unterminated last line checked) and exits 1 if any, 0 if none"
Run:
```
node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js "$d/bad.jsonl" > "$d/out" 2>&1; echo "bad exit=$?"; cat "$d/out"
grep -E "^$d/bad.jsonl:[0-9]+: .+" "$d/out" | sed "s|^$d/bad.jsonl:\([0-9]*\): .*|\1|" | tr '\n' ' '; echo
node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js "$d/clean.jsonl" > "$d/out2" 2>&1; echo "clean exit=$?"; cat "$d/out2"
node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js "$d/clean-noeol.jsonl"; echo "noeol exit=$?"
```
PASS if all hold: `bad exit=1`; the grep/sed line prints exactly `3 6 ` (one `<file>:<line>: <error>` line each for lines 3 and 6, with `<file>` equal to the path as passed and a non-empty error text, and no such line for any other line number); the output is not a Node crash (no stack trace / ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND); `clean exit=0` with no `<file>:<n>: ` line in its output; `noeol exit=0`. FAIL if any of these does not hold (for example exit 1 from a crash, a missing line 6 report, wrong line numbers, or blank lines reported).

Check 2 — expect line: "A missing file or no argument prints to stderr and exits 2"
Run:
```
node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js "$d/does-not-exist.jsonl" > "$d/o3" 2> "$d/e3"; echo "missing exit=$?"; echo "stderr:"; cat "$d/e3"
node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js > "$d/o4" 2> "$d/e4"; echo "noarg exit=$?"; echo "stderr:"; cat "$d/e4"
```
PASS if both cases print `exit=2` and each has non-empty stderr. FAIL if either exit code is not 2 or either stderr is empty.

Check 3 — expect line: "packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js exports lint(text) returning [{ line, error }]"
Run:
```
node --input-type=module -e "import { lint } from './packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js'; console.log(JSON.stringify(lint('{\"a\":1}\n\n{bad\n[1]\n{\"x\":'))); console.log(JSON.stringify(lint('{\"a\":1}\n')));"
```
PASS if the command exits 0, the first printed value is an array of two objects each with a numeric `line` and a non-empty string `error`, with `line` values 3 and 5, and the second printed value is `[]`. FAIL if the import fails, `lint` is not a named export, the return is not an array of `{ line, error }` objects, or the line values differ.

Check 4 — expect line: "The workspace has its own package.json (jsonl-lint, type module, test script node --test), no runtime dependencies, and node:test tests for a clean file, a bad middle row, a torn last row, blank lines and the exit codes"
Run:
```
node -e "const p=require('./packages/jsonl-lint/package.json'); console.log(JSON.stringify({name:p.name,type:p.type,test:p.scripts&&p.scripts.test,dependencies:p.dependencies}))"
npm test -w packages/jsonl-lint; echo "ws test exit=$?"
```
Then open the test files under `packages/jsonl-lint/` that the run executed.
PASS if: `name` is `jsonl-lint`, `type` is `module`, `test` is `node --test` (optionally followed by arguments); `dependencies` is absent or empty; `ws test exit=0` with 0 failing tests; and the executed tests import from `node:test` and include tests that exercise each of: a clean file, a bad middle row, a torn (unterminated, invalid) last row, blank lines, and the CLI exit codes (at least 0, 1 and 2 are asserted). FAIL if any field differs, there is a non-empty `dependencies`, the workspace tests fail or do not run, or any of the five test cases is missing.

Check 5 — expect line: "packages/jsonl-lint/README.md exists and the root README lists the tool"
Run:
```
test -f packages/jsonl-lint/README.md && echo readme-ok; grep -n 'jsonl-lint' README.md
```
PASS if `readme-ok` is printed and grep shows at least one line of the root `README.md` naming the jsonl-lint tool in its list of tools. FAIL if the file is missing or the root README does not mention it.

Check 6 — expect line: "The change is one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body says Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102, and npm test and the test workflow are green at its head"
Run:
```
gh api 'repos/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/pulls?state=open&per_page=100' --jq '[.[] | select((.body // "") | contains("Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102")) | {number, sha: .head.sha, ref: .head.ref}]'
sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD); gh api "repos/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/commits/$sha/check-runs" --jq '[.check_runs[] | {name, status, conclusion}]'
npm ci && npm test; echo "root exit=$?"
```
PASS if: the first command lists exactly one open PR, its body contains `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102`, and its `sha` equals the checked-out HEAD; the check runs for that sha include the `test` workflow job with status `completed` and conclusion `success` (and none failed); and `root exit=0` with the jsonl-lint tests run and passing. FAIL if there is no such PR or more than one, the body lacks the line, the head sha differs, the test workflow is missing, still running, or not successful, or `npm ci`/`npm test` fails.

Advisory (not part of PASS/FAIL):
- Error lines are expected on stdout and nothing on stdout for a clean file; note if they go to stderr instead.
- Note whether CRLF files and whitespace-only lines are handled sensibly, whether `bin/jsonl-lint.js` has a shebang and executable bit and a `bin` entry in package.json, and whether `package-lock.json` was updated for the new workspace.
- Note whether tests resolve paths from `import.meta.url` and clean up temp files.
